clue.text: Small change in look undesirable

parts.note: L stands for little, so small, a common crossword abbreviation

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of the synonym for look

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: A tiny alteration in appearance is something nobody wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undesirable' is read as a noun: a person shunned by others. 'change' rearranges PEER into EPER.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast whom everyone avoids is figuratively a shunned person, so an undesirable can be called this.

clue.text: Crucial helper flies around state

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of flies are moved about into a new order

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Someone who matters most to a project buzzes about the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal on 'flies'; 'state' is a verb meaning declare, not a country or region.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rescues you at a vital moment is figuratively a vital helper; the word also names a lifeguard.

clue.text: Start of avarice in human, one story's representation

parts.note: a human being is a person
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in tells us the first letter of avarice goes inside the story word

parts.note: a story is a piece of fiction

indicators.note: start of means take only the first letter of avarice

explanation.surface: A tale of a greedy man becomes a symbol of the vice itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' signal puts the first letter of 'avarice' inside the story word, not inside 'human'.
explanation.definitionFit: Embodying an abstract quality in a figure is a way of representing it, as Greed shown as a man.

clue.text: Stray shoe missing upper

indicators.note: in a down clue the upper letter is the first one, which is dropped from the shoe word

parts.note: a brogue is a stout leather shoe

explanation.surface: A lost shoe that has come apart, with no upper attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upper' is the part of a shoe above the sole, but here it means the top letter of a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray animal, such as an elephant living apart from its herd, is described this way; the word is an adjective there.

clue.text: Ready to fly toy starting with a whirr

indicators.note: starting, in the sense of jumping or jolting, signals the letters are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: A model plane that buzzes into life is set for take-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' is the anagram signal working on TOY, A and WHIRR; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft certified fit and safe for flight is described with this term.

clue.text: Casually, drunk don gets into a people-carrier

indicators.note: gets into means the scrambled letters go inside the other words

parts.note: a tram carries passengers along a street

indicators.note: drunk indicates the letters of don are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tipsy university lecturer boards a vehicle full of passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles 'don' to NDO, which 'gets into' places inside the vehicle. A don is a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something haphazardly, without plan or method, is doing it casually.

clue.text: European overwhelmed by noise in railway with congestion

indicators.note: in means the combined letters sit inside the railway abbreviation
overwhelmed by means the European letter is swallowed up by the noise word

parts.note: a hum is a low continuous noise

explanation.surface: A traveller on a noisy train is swamped by the din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelmed by' gives HEUM, the European letter inside the noise; 'in' then places it within the railway abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Watery, catarrhal eyes or a streaming nose mark someone suffering from a cold's blocked-up state.

clue.text: Old boy requiring help to be aware of surroundings

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a help is a domestic servant

explanation.surface: An elderly man who needs assistance to know what is going on around him.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchful person notices what goes on around them, being quick to take things in.

clue.text: Eden folk were got badly by this

definitions.text: Eden folk were got badly by this

indicators.note: badly signals the four preceding words are jumbled together into a new order

explanation.surface: Adam and Eve came to grief through one particular plant in Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of EDEN FOLK WERE GOT also describes the answer: Genesis tells how the first couple were undone by eating its fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the forbidden fruit grew on this plant, and eating from it led to the expulsion from paradise.

clue.text: An age is number to get blue about in retrospect

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the whole thing is read backwards
about means the blue word goes round the number abbreviation

parts.note: the sky is blue, a common crossword equation

explanation.surface: Getting depressed over a figure that has been around for ever, looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' first makes SKNOY, which 'in retrospect' turns round. The answer is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal slang for a very long time, matching the idiom of waiting an age.

clue.text: Pro nurses storm one gathering

indicators.note: nurses means holds within, so the pro word wraps round the storm word

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so for
to rage is to storm

explanation.surface: A professional cares for patients while a storm gathers outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like a medical noun but is a verb meaning holds within, the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who searches for and collects wild food is a gatherer.

clue.text: Oriental festival's name

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival

explanation.surface: What a festival from the Far East is called.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from Asia or the Orient lies to the east, so it is described with this direction word.

clue.text: Trick played on masked apes

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are toyed with into a new arrangement

parts.note: to ape someone is to copy or reflect them, as a looking glass does

explanation.surface: A prank is pulled on monkeys wearing disguises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges ON MASKED into the first two words; 'apes' is a verb meaning imitates.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means deception or illusion intended to distract, as in a conjuror's trick.

clue.text: Source of sound coming from very old freezer

parts.note: an icebox is a freezer or old-fashioned fridge

explanation.surface: A noise is coming from an ancient fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx is the organ in the throat that produces speech and other vocal sound.

clue.text: Worked out decree is wrong, getting cross inwardly

indicators.note: inwardly means the cross letter goes inside the scrambled letters
wrong signals the letters of decree and is are put in a new order

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A decree is flawed and someone gets angry inside about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' scrambles the first two words and 'inwardly' sets the cross letter within. 'cross' looks like anger but is the shape of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise is to take physical exercise, so having trained at the gym is the same as having done a workout.

clue.text: Take over request for engineering part

indicators.note: over means the take word sits over and around the request word

parts.note: to take something is to get it
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Someone asks to take charge of an engineering component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take over' reads as one phrase meaning assume control; split up, 'over' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal fitted between two surfaces of an engine or pipe joint is a component in machinery.

clue.text: Stained metal better cut with tool's head

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: cut with means a letter breaks into the cured word

parts.note: cured means made well again, recovered: better

indicators.note: head means the first letter of tool

explanation.surface: A dirty piece of metal is improved by cutting with the end of a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is an adjective meaning recovered from illness, not a verb meaning improve.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured or tinged with a dye or pigment, as a liquid or cloth can be.

clue.text: Fix top on vessel for islander

parts.note: a jam is a fix or tight spot
A1 means first-rate or top, written AI
a can is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: Put a lid on a container for someone from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' means excellent: A1, with the 1 written as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a Caribbean island nation lives on that island.

clue.text: One overturning animal's home after game's shot

indicators.note: after puts the one and overturned home behind the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: overturning means the home word is turned backwards

parts.note: a den is a wild animal's home

explanation.surface: A hunter's shot ruins an animal's lair after a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like part of the hunting picture but is the definition: wrecked, as in 'my nerves are shot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is shot, informally, is wrecked beyond repair, completely destroyed.

clue.text: Hotel throw a wobbly with new fruit supplier

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: wobbly suggests the letters of throw a are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A hotel guest throws a tantrum with a new greengrocer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw a wobbly' is British for having a tantrum; here 'wobbly' rearranges THROW A between H and N.
explanation.definitionFit: This thorny shrub bears red berries called haws, so it supplies fruit.

clue.text: Structure outdoors life around navigational aid with live upgrade

indicators.note: around means the life word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: go means energy, vitality, life
an A-Z is a street map book for finding one's way

indicators.note: upgrade in a down clue means reading upwards, so the live word is written backwards

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A garden building needs a better sat-nav and a live software update.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upgrade' means read upwards. An A-Z is a British street atlas, and 'life' means vitality.
explanation.definitionFit: A summerhouse or open pavilion in a garden is a building set in the open air.

clue.text: Greeting Davina, some might say it's unmemorable thing

indicators.note: some might say means the words are spoken aloud to give a similar-sounding word

parts.note: wotcha is a casual British greeting; Davina McCall is a British TV presenter
taken as written, ignoring the 's

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a TV presenter you have forgotten the name of.
explanation.walkthrough: Davina McCall is a British television presenter; 'Wotcha' is a casual London hello.
explanation.definitionFit: A placeholder word used for an object whose proper name escapes you, like thingummy.

clue.text: Beat two jockeys over races, expert overlooked

indicators.note: over means the scrambled letters go round the remains of races
jockeys as a verb means manoeuvres or jostles, so the letters of two change places
overlooked means left out, so the expert word is dropped from races

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A pair of riders win as they race, ignoring the expert's view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockeys' is a verb meaning jostles, making WOT; 'overlooked' leaves RS from 'races'.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the better of an opponent and defeat them is a sense of the verb meaning beat.

clue.text: Mature broad ultimately content

indicators.note: content means the contents, the letters held inside broad ultimately

explanation.surface: A grown-up woman is happy in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like happy, but it means what is contained.
explanation.definitionFit: Fully grown and mature describe the same state; a grown-up is the noun counterpart.

clue.text: Again, send out note prior to me fetching kids

parts.note: in tonic sol-fa, re comes just before mi, the note sounded me
issue means children or offspring

explanation.surface: Someone sends a note before collecting their children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the sol-fa note usually written mi, so the note before it is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out or publish once more, as a stamp or album, is to send it out a second time.

clue.text: Heave grouse, having died over time

indicators.note: having died over time means the died letter takes over from the time letter

parts.note: to chunter is to grumble or grouse

explanation.surface: A moorland bird struggles up, having perished after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' is a grumble here, not the game bird. 'Heave' means vomit; the answer is Australian slang for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaving in the sense of retching or throwing up matches this Australian slang word for vomiting.

clue.text: Modest community nets a large cup

indicators.note: nets means catches, so the community word holds the other pieces

parts.note: a town is a community
a means one
DD is a large bra cup size

explanation.surface: A local town wins a big trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cup' looks like a trophy but is a bra size, and 'a' stands for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made less extreme or showy has been moderated, as a modest version is.

clue.text: Daughter after precious material

indicators.note: after places the daughter letter behind the precious word

parts.note: precious means affectedly dainty: twee

explanation.surface: A girl comes after costly fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precious' means affectedly sweet here, not valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough woollen cloth from Scotland is a kind of fabric.
